title: Left re-indexing preserves circuit evaluation
statement: Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m_1$ variables, and let $g_1 : \mathrm{Fin}\,m_1 \to \bbf_2$ and $g_2 : \mathrm{Fin}\,m_2 \to \bbf_2$ be assignments. Write $\iota : \mathrm{Fin}\,m_1 \to \mathrm{Fin}\,(m_1+m_2)$, $i \mapsto i$, for the order-preserving inclusion of the first block, and let $g$ be the merged assignment on $m_1 + m_2$ variables that agrees with $g_1$ on the first $m_1$ indices and with $g_2$ on the last $m_2$. Then the circuit obtained by replacing each literal index $i$ of $c$ by $\iota(i)$ (keeping its sign), evaluated under $g$, has the same value as $c$ evaluated under $g_1$.
hypotheses_covered: c is a Boolean circuit on m₁ variables
g₁ is an assignment on Fin m₁
g₂ is an assignment on Fin m₂
re-indexing along the left inclusion ι = Fin.castAdd, i ↦ i
evaluation under the merged assignment of g₁ and g₂
replaced:
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m_1$ variables, and let $g_1 : \mathrm{Fin}\,m_1 \to
\mathrm{Bool}$ and $g_2 : \mathrm{Fin}\,m_2 \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be Boolean arrays.
Re-index $c$ along the left inclusion $\mathrm{Fin}\,m_1 \to \mathrm{Fin}\,(m_1+m_2)$,
$i \mapsto i$, which sends each literal index $i$ to the same index $i$ in the enlarged
range and keeps its sign. Then evaluating the re-indexed circuit under the merged array
$\mathrm{mergeGates}\,g_1\,g_2$ gives the same Boolean value as evaluating $c$ under
$g_1$.
